title: Joel Mokyr, who grew up in Haifa, explained what drives sustained growth and won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Economics

trailer.text: Joel Mokyr, an Israeli-American economist and professor of economics and history at Northwestern University, was born in Leiden in the Netherlands to a Dutch-Jewish family that survived the Holocaust, and was raised in Haifa.
Mokyr described his research as an inquiry into why we are so much richer and live so much better than our great-great-grandfathers.
In the 1990s he used historical sources to uncover the causes of sustained growth.

He showed that if innovations are to succeed one another in a self-generating process, scientific explanations for why the innovations work are needed, and he also emphasized the importance of society being open to new ideas and to change.
For this he received half of the 2025 Nobel Prize in Economics.

paragraphs.text: Mokyr was born in Leiden in the Netherlands to a family of Dutch Jews who survived the Holocaust.
When he was one year old, his father died of cancer.
His mother immigrated with him to Israel and raised him in Haifa.
He studied economics and history at the Hebrew University.
In 1968 he completed a bachelor's degree there with honors.
In the early 1970s Mokyr studied at Yale under the supervision of William Parker.
Richard Levin, his fellow doctoral student, said Mokyr arrived there already determined to be an economic historian.
His doctoral dissertation dealt with industrialization and economic development in the Netherlands and Belgium in 1800–1850.
In 1974 he received a PhD in economics from Yale.
Today he is a professor of economics and history at Northwestern and holds the Robert H. Strotz chair.
The chair of the economics department there said Mokyr has spent more than 50 years at the institution.
He is an expert on the economic history of Europe, specializing in the period 1750–1914.
His connection to Israel also continues.
Since 2001, he has also been a Sackler research fellow at the Eitan Berglas School of Economics at Tel Aviv University.
The dean of the Faculty of Social Sciences in Tel Aviv said Mokyr regularly teaches there as a visiting lecturer.
According to the Department of Economics at Northwestern University, Mokyr has been a member of the department since 1974.

stations.title: The question: why do we live better?

paragraphs.text: Over the last two centuries the world has seen sustained economic growth, but this was not always the case.
According to the prize committee, economic stagnation, not growth, was the norm for most of human history.
According to NPR, growth was flat for millennia, and then, around 1800, shot upward.
Mokyr said that 150 years ago life expectancy was less than 40.
He said that today life expectancy in the world is 73 for women and 68 for men.
According to CEPR, over the past two centuries innovations that raised living standards have lifted billions out of poverty.
Mokyr described his research as an inquiry into why we are so much richer and live so much better than our great-great-grandfathers.
In the 1990s he used historical sources to uncover the causes of sustained growth.

stations.title: The answer: knowledge, hands and institutions

paragraphs.text: Mokyr explained that the inventions that preceded the technological revolution lacked scientific explanations, and that without them innovation is hard to replicate.
According to mako, before the Industrial Revolution, without scientific explanations, people struggled to build on earlier discoveries.
Mokyr showed that if innovations are to succeed one another in a self-generating process, scientific explanations for why they work are needed.
He identified three important requisites for growth: useful knowledge, mechanical competence and institutions conducive to technological progress.
He also emphasized the importance of society being open to new ideas and to change.
His research showed how culture, knowledge and institutions create fertile ground for innovation.
Mokyr describes the Industrial Revolution as a clustering of macro-inventions that led to an acceleration of micro-inventions.
According to CEPR, political fragmentation in Europe undermined the ability of authoritarian rulers to suppress ideas.
According to CEPR, China's rigid political unity stifled technical change, and at times even reversed it.
According to NPR, his research suggests that Britain was different because, essentially, the British applied the Enlightenment in the real economy more than other nations.
His book, A Culture of Growth, asks what made the Industrial Revolution possible, and how culture influenced it.
His latest book, written with Avner Greif and Guido Tabellini, on culture and institutions in China and Europe, was published in November 2025 by Princeton University Press.
The Royal Swedish Academy announced that the prize had been awarded to Israeli-American Joel Mokyr and two other researchers.
Mokyr receives half of the prize for developing a theory of sustained economic growth.
The other half went to Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt for creating a mathematical model.
In a 1992 article they built a mathematical model of creative destruction.
According to JNS, Mokyr was at his vacation home in Western Michigan when he got the news.
He said there was a missed call on his phone from Sweden.
He said he went to the computer to see who had won, out of curiosity, and then found a congratulatory message.
He said he had a long list of people who deserved to win.
Mokyr said that at the time he was preoccupied with the news of the release of the Israeli hostages.
He said his heart beats with joy at their return.
He said he has an Israeli passport, that an Israeli heart beats in him, and that the prize also says something about Israel.
According to the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, the 2025 prize in economics is 11 million Swedish kronor, and half of it was awarded to Joel Mokyr.

stations.title: What was said in Stockholm, and what came before

paragraphs.text: Prize citation: for having identified the prerequisites for sustained growth through technological progress.
According to Tel Aviv University, the Swedish Academy emphasized that such progress should not be taken for granted.
The chair of the prize committee said that economic growth cannot be taken for granted, and that the mechanisms of creative destruction must be upheld so as not to fall back into stagnation.
He is the fourth Yale-trained Nobel laureate in economics in the past four years.
The Nobel was not the first recognition.
In 2006 he won the Heineken Award for History of the Royal Dutch Academy of Sciences.
In 2015 he won the International Balzan Prize for his work on the economic history of Europe.
Each Balzan Prize winner received about 750,000 Swiss francs.
In 2018 he was named a Distinguished Fellow of the American Economic Association.
That same year he won the Elinor Ostrom Prize for a paper he wrote with Avner Greif.
According to CEPR, Mokyr has written thirteen books and more than one hundred articles, and edited a five-volume encyclopedia.
According to CEPR, many of his doctoral students are intellectual leaders in their own right.
A former student said he could not have succeeded without Mokyr, and that his case is not unusual.
Economist Uri Katz, who studied with him, said he is one of the best lecturers he has heard.
Katz said Mokyr belongs to a new generation that brought cultural and institutional factors into economics.
According to him, the Industrial Revolution happened in Europe because of competition between the states, which prevented pressure groups from stopping progress.
Northwestern's president said Mokyr has had a profound impact on the understanding of economics and history by incorporating culture into the analysis of economic growth.
The dean of the Faculty of Social Sciences in Tel Aviv said the win is further evidence of the prestige of Israeli research worldwide.
Northwestern said Mokyr's optimistic perspectives are widely cited in major media.
Mokyr said he is optimistic about continued growth, because of the human capability to harness the forces of nature to its own needs.
In a 2018 interview with Globes he said that most human societies did not believe in progress.
That same year he said there is a broad feeling that technological improvements serve a small group at the expense of the rest.
He also said he is less optimistic about the survival of democracy and open institutions.
In a January 2024 interview he said that institutional progress has not kept up with technological progress, and that we have not learned to avoid wars.
Mokyr was among the economists who signed the letters warning of the economic consequences of the judicial reform the government began promoting in 2023.

claims.text: מוקיר זכה בפרס בלזן הבינלאומי ב-2015 על עבודתו בהיסטוריה הכלכלית של אירופה.
claims.quote: He was awarded the prestigious International Balzan Prize for his groundbreaking work on the economic history of Europe and roots of technological change in 2015.

claims.text: ב-2018 מוקיר מונה לעמית מכובד של האגודה הכלכלית האמריקנית.
claims.quote: In 2018, Mokyr was named a Distinguished Fellow of the American Economic Association

claims.text: מוקיר זכה בפרס אלינור אוסטרום לשנת 2018 על מאמר שכתב עם אבנר גרייף.
claims.quote: Mokyr was awarded the 2018 Elinor Ostrom Prize for the paper

claims.text: לפי mako, מוקיר זכה בעבר בפרס בלצן.
claims.quote: הוא גם זכה בעבר בפרס בלצן, המוענק מדי שנה למצטיינים יוצאי דופן במדעי הרוח, הטבע והתרבות

claims.text: כל זוכה בפרס בלזן קיבל כ-750,000 פרנק שוויצרי.
claims.quote: Each prize winner was awarded approximately 750,000 Swiss Francs (approximately $770,000).

claims.text: לפי CEPR, למוקיר יותר מ-60 דוקטורנטים, רבים מהם מנהיגים אינטלקטואליים בזכות עצמם.
claims.quote: has come through his more than 60 doctoral students, many of whom have become intellectual leaders in their own right

claims.text: תלמיד לשעבר אמר שלא היה מצליח בלי מוקיר, ושמקרהו אינו חריג.
claims.quote: It is not an exaggeration to say that I could not have done it without Joel

claims.text: אורי כץ, שלמד אצל מוקיר, אמר שהוא אחד המרצים הטובים ביותר ששמע.
claims.quote: יואל מוקיר היה אחר, הוא באמת אחד המרצים הכי טובים שיצא לי לשמוע

claims.text: הכלכלן אורי כץ אמר שמוקיר שייך לדור חדש שהכניס לכלכלה גורמים תרבותיים ומוסדיים.
claims.quote: מוקיר, לעומת זאת, שייך לדור חדש שהכניס לתוך הכלכלה גורמים תרבותיים ומוסדיים

claims.text: לדברי אורי כץ, המהפכה התעשייתית קרתה באירופה בגלל תחרות בין המדינות שמנעה מקבוצות לחץ לעצור את הקדמה.
claims.quote: המהפכה התעשייתית קרתה באירופה מפני שבין המדינות שם התקיימה תחרות בלתי פוסקת, שלא אפשרה לקבוצות לחץ לעצור את הקדמה

claims.text: נשיא נורת'ווסטרן אמר שלמוקיר היתה השפעה עמוקה על ההבנה של כלכלה והיסטוריה, בכך ששילב תרבות בניתוח הצמיחה הכלכלית.
claims.quote: he has had a profound impact on our understanding of both economics and history by incorporating culture into the analysis of economic growth

claims.text: דיקאן הפקולטה למדעי החברה בתל אביב אמר שהזכייה היא עדות נוספת ליוקרת המחקר הישראלי בעולם.
claims.quote: זו עדות נוספת ליוקרתו של המחקר הישראלי בעולם ולמעמדו הרם של בית הספר לכלכלה

claims.text: נורת'ווסטרן מסרה שהתפיסות האופטימיות של מוקיר מצוטטות רבות בתקשורת הגדולה.
claims.quote: his optimistic perspectives have been widely cited by major media outlets

claims.text: מוקיר אמר שהוא אופטימי לגבי המשך הצמיחה בגלל יכולת האדם לרתום את כוחות הטבע לצרכיו.
claims.quote: human capability of manipulating and harnessing the forces of nature to its own needs

claims.text: בראיון לגלובס ב-2018 אמר מוקיר שרוב החברות האנושיות לא האמינו בקידמה.
claims.quote: Most human societies that have ever existed did not believe in progress

claims.text: מוקיר אמר ב-2018 שיש תחושה רחבה שהשיפורים הטכנולוגיים משרתים קבוצה קטנה על חשבון השאר.
claims.quote: There is a feeling among very broad strata that technological improvements serve a small group, which is getting richer and stronger at the expense of the rest

claims.text: מוקיר אמר ב-2018 שהוא פחות אופטימי לגבי הישרדות הדמוקרטיה והמוסדות הפתוחים.
claims.quote: Today I am starting to think that I am right about technologies, and less optimistic about the survival of democracy and open institutions, including globalization.

claims.text: בראיון בינואר 2024 אמר מוקיר שהקידמה המוסדית לא הדביקה את הקידמה הטכנולוגית ושלא למדנו להימנע ממלחמות.
claims.quote: The problem is that with technological progress, institutional progress has not followed. We have failed to teach ourselves how to avoid wars.

claims.text: מוקיר היה בין הכלכלנים שחתמו על מכתבים שהזהירו מהשלכות כלכליות של המהפכה המשפטית של 2023.
claims.quote: Prof. Mokyr was among the economists who signed the letters warning of the economic consequences of the judicial reform the government began promoting in 2023.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, מוקיר הנחה כ-40 דוקטורנטים.
claims.quote: He has supervised around 40 doctoral students, and his relationships with them are known to be close and ongoing.

claims.text: לפי ynet, מוקיר הנחה או הנחה במשותף יותר מ-50 דוקטורנטים.
claims.quote: במהלך הקריירה שלו הנחה או היה שותף בהנחיית יותר מ-50 סטודנטים לדוקטורט

claims.text: mako כינה אותו "הישראלי לשעבר" יואל מוקיר.
claims.quote: הישראלי לשעבר יואל מוקיר זכה בפרס נובל לכלכלה לשנת 2025

claims.text: לפי האקדמיה המלכותית השוודית למדעים, סכום הפרס בכלכלה לשנת 2025 הוא 11 מיליון קרונות שוודיות, ומחציתו ניתנה ליואל מוקיר.
claims.quote: Prize amount: 11 million Swedish kronor

claims.text: לפי המחלקה לכלכלה באוניברסיטת נורת'ווסטרן, מוקיר חבר במחלקה מאז 1974.
claims.quote: Mokyr has been with the Department of Economics since 1974.

claims.text: ספרו האחרון, שכתב עם אבנר גרייף וגידו טבליני, על תרבות ומוסדות בסין ובאירופה, יצא בנובמבר 2025 בהוצאת פרינסטון.
claims.quote: Avner Greif, Joel Mokyr, and Guido Tabellini
